views.name: lap_times_with_driver_and_race
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  lapTimes.raceId AS "lapTimes.raceId",
  lapTimes.driverId AS "lapTimes.driverId",
  lapTimes.lap AS "lapTimes.lap",
  lapTimes.milliseconds AS "lapTimes.milliseconds",
  lapTimes.time AS "lapTimes.time",
  drivers.forename AS "drivers.forename",
  drivers.surname AS "drivers.surname",
  races.name AS "races.name",
  lapTimes.raceId AS raceId,
  lapTimes.driverId AS driverId,
  lapTimes.lap AS lap
FROM lapTimes
JOIN drivers ON drivers.driverId = lapTimes.driverId
JOIN races ON races.raceId = lapTimes.raceId

params.description: Provides lap-level timing records enriched with the driver name and race name (one row per raceId, driverId, lap).
params.when_to_use: Show or filter lap times for a specific race, driver, or lap (e.g., list all laps for driver X in race Y). | Compare lap times across drivers within a race or track a single driver's lap progression across laps. | Use as a base to compute further aggregates (e.g., average lap time per driver in a race) by aggregating over its lap-level rows. | Join with dimensions that are one-to-one with raceId or driverId to add additional descriptive attributes without duplicating lap rows.
params.output_schema: lapTimes.raceId: race identifier (from lapTimes.raceId) | lapTimes.driverId: driver identifier (from lapTimes.driverId) | lapTimes.lap: lap number within the race (from lapTimes.lap) | lapTimes.milliseconds: lap time in milliseconds (from lapTimes.milliseconds) | lapTimes.time: lap time as formatted string (from lapTimes.time) | drivers.forename: driver's forename (from drivers.forename via join on drivers.driverId = lapTimes.driverId) | drivers.surname: driver's surname (from drivers.surname via join on drivers.driverId = lapTimes.driverId) | races.name: race name (from races.name via join on races.raceId = lapTimes.raceId)
params.grounded_columns: lapTimes.raceId | lapTimes.driverId | lapTimes.lap | lapTimes.milliseconds | lapTimes.time | drivers.forename | drivers.surname | races.name
params.metric: This view exposes no pre-computed aggregates; all columns are raw/persisted base columns from the joined tables. | Derived aggregate examples you can compute from this view (NOT precomputed here): | avg_lap_milliseconds = AVG(lapTimes.milliseconds) grouped by (lapTimes.raceId, lapTimes.driverId) -- compute by aggregating rows of this view | min_lap_milliseconds = MIN(lapTimes.milliseconds) grouped by (lapTimes.raceId) -- compute by aggregating rows of this view
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE: join to driver_dim on lapTimes.driverId = driver_dim.driverId — safe because this view is one row per (raceId, driverId, lap) and driver_dim is one row per driverId; joining will not duplicate lap rows. | cardinality-SAFE: join to race_basic on lapTimes.raceId = race_basic.raceId — safe because race_basic is one row per raceId; joining will not duplicate lap rows. | cardinality-SAFE: join to constructor_dim on lapTimes.driverId = constructor_dim.driverId ONLY IF constructor_dim is modeled one-to-one per driverId; safe when constructor_dim has at most one row per driverId. | DO NOT join this view directly to one-to-many fact/aggregate views (for example: driver_lap_aggregates, pitstop_aggregates, fastest_lap_per_race, season_driver_points) without re-aggregating or otherwise controlling cardinality — those joins can multiply lap rows and thus duplicate/over-count any metrics computed at the lap grain. | If you need to combine a lap-level measure with a multi-row-per-(raceId,driverId) aggregate, first aggregate the other source to the same grain as this view (raceId, driverId, lap OR typically to raceId+driverId if lap-level alignment isn't required), or aggregate this view up to the desired grain before joining. | When composing SQL planners should treat this view as having grain = (lapTimes.raceId, lapTimes.driverId, lapTimes.lap). Any join that is many-to-one from this view's grain to a dimension is safe; any join that is one-to-many from this view's grain will multiply rows and requires aggregation to avoid measure duplication.

views.name: driver_results

SELECT

params.when_to_use: Retrieve individual race result rows for drivers (e.g., list all results for a driver or a race). | Compose driver-level or race-level aggregations (sum of points, counts of podiums) by aggregating this view. | Join result-level attributes onto other result-level or one-row-per-race/driver reference data for reporting or further aggregation. | Build season summaries by aggregating points/positions per driver per year (must aggregate this view; do not join raw one-to-many detail afterwards).
params.output_schema: resultId: unique identifier for the race result row, derived from race_results_enriched.resultId | raceId: identifier of the race for this result, derived from race_results_enriched.raceId | driverId: identifier of the driver for this result, derived from race_results_enriched.driverId | position: numeric finishing position for the result (nullable if not classified), derived from race_results_enriched.position | points: numeric points awarded for this result, derived from race_results_enriched.points | positionText: textual representation of finishing position (e.g., 'R' for retired), derived from race_results_enriched.positionText | year: season year in which the race took place, derived from race_results_enriched.year

params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to driver_dim on driverId — safe because driver_dim is one-row-per-driver (this view is one-row-per-result and will not have its measures duplicated when enriching with driver attributes). | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to race_basic on raceId — safe because race_basic is one-row-per-race (enriching result rows with race attributes will not duplicate measures). | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to constructor_dim on constructorId only after ensuring a single constructorId per result row (this view does not expose constructorId; if constructorId exists in a sibling view with one-row-per-result it is safe; do not join constructor_dim to a multi-row-per-result source). | do NOT join directly to driver_lap_aggregates, pitstop_aggregates, fastest_lap_per_race, qualifying_grid_positions, or any AGG/JOIN views that are one-to-many per result (e.g., multiple laps, multiple pitstops) without re-aggregating or restricting to a single row per result first — such joins would multiply this view's rows and therefore duplicate points and other measures. | when composing season-level metrics (for example, total points per driver per year), aggregate this view (e.g., SUM(points) GROUP BY driverId, year) rather than joining this view to detailed lap/pitstop tables and then aggregating, to avoid double-counting. | if you must join to a one-to-many detail (laps, pitstops), perform the aggregation on the detail first to a matching grain (e.g., per resultId) and then join that aggregated result back to this view on resultId — that preserves cardinality and prevents duplication of points/positions.

views.name: driver_core
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  driverId,
  trim(COALESCE(forename, '') || CASE WHEN forename IS NOT NULL AND surname IS NOT NULL THEN ' ' ELSE '' END || COALESCE(surname, '')) AS full_name,
  nationality,
  driverRef,
  dob,
  code
FROM drivers

params.description: Provides one-row-per-driver core attributes (identifiers and demographic/lookup fields) for composing driver-level queries and joins.
params.when_to_use: Lookup a driver's canonical attributes (name, reference code, nationality, date of birth) by driverId or driverRef. | Join driver attributes onto driver-level aggregated metrics (points, wins, laps, pitstops) without changing cardinality. | Compose driver-level reports per season/race by joining this view to aggregated or ranked driver-level views. | Display driver metadata in UIs, labels, or export files alongside computed measures from aggregation views.
params.output_schema: driverId: unique identifier for a driver (from drivers.driverId). Use this as the primary key / join key for driver-level compositions. | full_name: trimmed concatenation of forename and surname (derived from drivers.forename and drivers.surname using trim and conditional space). | nationality: driver's nationality (from drivers.nationality). | driverRef: short reference code/name for the driver (from drivers.driverRef). | dob: date of birth (from drivers.dob). | code: three-letter or short code for the driver (from drivers.code).
params.grounded_columns: drivers.driverId | drivers.forename | drivers.surname | drivers.nationality | drivers.driverRef | drivers.dob | drivers.code
params.metric: driverId = drivers.driverId | full_name = trim(coalesce(drivers.forename, '') || CASE WHEN drivers.forename IS NOT NULL AND drivers.surname IS NOT NULL THEN ' ' ELSE '' END || coalesce(drivers.surname, '')) | nationality = drivers.nationality | driverRef = drivers.driverRef | dob = drivers.dob | code = drivers.code
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to driver_dim on driverId — safe because driver_core is one-row-per-driver (driverId is the grain) so joining driver_dim (a dimension keyed by driverId) will not duplicate rows from driver_core. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to season_driver_points or driver_lap_aggregates or driver_season_rank on driverId (and season when present) — these are aggregated one-row-per-(driverId[, season]) views, so when joined back to driver_core by driverId (and season if included) they will not duplicate driver_core rows as long as you preserve the aggregation grain (i.e., join on both driverId and season if the aggregate is per-season). | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to race_results_enriched on driverId and raceId — safe when race_results_enriched is intended as one-row-per-(raceId, driverId); however, that join will expand driver_core into multiple rows (one per race) which is expected when composing race-level outputs. This expansion is not duplication of measures in race-level results but is a multiplication of the driver row for per-race analysis. | do NOT join driver_core directly to one-to-many event-level raw tables (e.g., raw lap-level tables) if you intend to preserve driver-level measures — such joins will multiply driver_core rows. Instead, first aggregate the one-to-many table to driver-level (or driverId+season/race level) and then join the aggregated result to driver_core. | do NOT join driver_core to pitstop_aggregates or fastest_lap_per_race without matching grains: if the aggregate is per-(driverId, raceId) or per-(driverId, season), include those keys in the join condition; otherwise you may inadvertently duplicate driver rows when an aggregate produces multiple rows per driver. | When composing measures, ensure joins use driverId as the primary key; if you must join by driverRef or code, validate these are unique in the drivers table for your dataset or join through driverId to avoid unexpected multiplicity.

views.description: Provides one-row-per-driver core attributes (identifiers and demographic/lookup fields) for composing driver-level queries and joins.

views.name: driver_wins_by_season_race
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  driverStandings.driverId AS driverId,
  driverStandings.raceId AS raceId,
  COALESCE(driverStandings.wins, 0) AS wins
FROM driverStandings

params.description: Counts of wins per driver in a specific race (one row per driverId x raceId).
params.when_to_use: Get how many race wins a driver has in a specific race (typically 0 or 1) for reporting or joining into season-level aggregates | Compose into driver-centric or race-centric summaries where per-driver-per-race win indicator is needed | Filter or aggregate wins by season, constructor, circuit, or other race dimensions by joining to race or driver dimensions
params.output_schema: driverId: identifier of the driver — derived from driverStandings.driverId | raceId: identifier of the race — derived from driverStandings.raceId | wins: number of wins for that driver in that race — derived from COALESCE(driverStandings.wins, 0)
params.grounded_columns: driverStandings.driverId | driverStandings.raceId | driverStandings.wins
params.metric: wins = COALESCE(driverStandings.wins, 0)  -- a grounded column (no further aggregation in this view); represents the wins count recorded in driverStandings for that driverId x raceId
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to driver_dim on driverId — safe because driver_dim is a dimension keyed 1:1 (or many:1 from this view) by driverId, so joining will not duplicate the wins measure. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to race_basic on raceId — safe because race_basic is a dimension keyed 1:1 by raceId, so joining will not duplicate the wins measure. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to constructor_dim via a driver or race keyed join (e.g., through driver_dim or race_basic) — safe when the join path is 1:1 or many:1 to the view's driverId/raceId keys. | unsafe-to-join-without-care: do NOT directly join to one-to-many detail tables or views (for example race_results_enriched, driver_lap_aggregates, pitstop_aggregates, fastest_lap_per_race, qualifying_grid_positions, driver_running_points_by_season, season_driver_points, season_constructor_points) on raceId or driverId unless you first aggregate those tables to the same grain (driverId x raceId or a superset) because those are one-to-many relative to this view and will multiply the wins measure. | unsafe example: do not join driver_lap_aggregates or pitstop_aggregates directly on raceId + driverId because they contain multiple rows per driver per race; instead aggregate them to driverId x raceId (e.g., SUM/lists) before joining so the wins values remain correct. | safe composition pattern: to get seasonal totals, aggregate this view (e.g., SUM(wins) GROUP BY driverId, season) after joining race_basic to bring in season, or join race_basic first and then aggregate by driverId and season — either approach preserves correctness because aggregation eliminates duplication risk. | note on joins to sibling AGG or RANK views: when joining to another aggregated view (e.g., season_driver_points, driver_season_rank), ensure both are at compatible grains. If the other AGG is at driver-season grain, either (A) aggregate this view to driver-season before joining, or (B) join through race_basic to align grains and then aggregate — otherwise you risk many-to-one duplication.

views.name: driver_points_events
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  ds.driverStandingsId AS source_row_id,
  ds.driverId AS driverId,
  ds.raceId AS raceId,
  ds.points AS points,
  'driverStandings' AS source_table
FROM driverStandings ds
WHERE ds.points IS NOT NULL

UNION ALL

SELECT
  r.resultId AS source_row_id,
  r.driverId AS driverId,
  r.raceId AS raceId,
  r.points AS points,
  'results' AS source_table
FROM results r
WHERE r.points IS NOT NULL

params.description: Union of per-driver-per-race points events coming from driverStandings and results, used to treat both sources as a single canonical stream of points records.
params.when_to_use: List all points awarded to drivers in a particular race (including both results and standings sources). | Aggregate driver points by race, season, or driver when you can treat each source-row as a separate points event (e.g., sum points). | Join driver-level or race-level attributes to points events for reporting or further aggregation (e.g., compute total points by driver for a season). | Compose into downstream aggregated views (season totals, per-driver race histories) where the granularity is driverId × raceId × source_row_id.
params.output_schema: driverId: the driver identifier for this points event; derived from driverStandings.driverId (for driverStandings rows) or results.driverId (for results rows). | raceId: the race identifier associated with this points event; derived from driverStandings.raceId (for driverStandings rows) or results.raceId (for results rows). | points: numeric points value for this event; derived from driverStandings.points (for driverStandings rows) or results.points (for results rows). | source_table: literal indicating origin of the row — 'driverStandings' for the first branch and 'results' for the second branch; useful to distinguish provenance. | source_row_id: the primary key id of the source row that produced this event; derived from driverStandings.driverStandingsId (for driverStandings rows) or results.resultId (for results rows).
params.grounded_columns: driverStandings.driverStandingsId | driverStandings.driverId | driverStandings.raceId | driverStandings.points | results.resultId | results.driverId | results.raceId | results.points
params.metric: points = raw event value (no transformation). Use SUM(points) when aggregating over a coarser grain (e.g., SUM(points) BY driverId, season). | count_events = COUNT(*) when counting source events at the view grain (driverId, raceId, source_row_id).
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to driver_dim on driverId — safe because driver_dim is a one-row-per-driver dimension; joining will not duplicate points events. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to race_basic on raceId — safe because race_basic is a one-row-per-race dimension; joining will not duplicate points events. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to constructor_dim via driver -> constructor if you first join driver_dim (one-to-one) and then constructor_dim (one-to-one); ensure the join path is driver_points_events.driverId = driver_dim.driverId THEN driver_dim.constructorId = constructor_dim.constructorId (both dimensions must be one-row-per-key). | do NOT join directly to any one-to-many fact or event-level table/view such as race_results_enriched, driver_lap_aggregates, pitstop_aggregates, fastest_lap_per_race, qualifying_grid_positions, season_driver_points, season_constructor_points, driver_season_rank, driver_running_points_by_season without re-aggregation — these are one-to-many relative to this view's grain and will multiply points rows and inflate SUM(points) unless you first aggregate the other side to the same grain (e.g., aggregate lap or pitstop metrics to driverId×raceId or to driverId×season before joining). | When composing into aggregated metrics, always aggregate driver_points_events to the target grain before joining to another one-to-many dataset, e.g., to get points per driver per season: SELECT driverId, seasonId, SUM(points) FROM driver_points_events JOIN race_basic USING (raceId) GROUP BY driverId, seasonId; this prevents duplicating points if race_basic were to be many-to-one (raceBasic is one-to-one, but pattern applies generally). | If you need to combine with another event-level source (e.g., results detail or lap-level data), perform aggregation on that source to driverId×raceId (or whichever lower grain you need) and then join on (driverId, raceId, source_row_id only if matching ids), or join only on (driverId, raceId) after aggregating to that key.

views.description: Union of per-driver-per-race points events coming from driverStandings and results, used to treat both sources as a single canonical stream of points records.

views.name: drivers_name_nationality
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  driverId,
  forename,
  surname,
  driverRef,
  number,
  code,
  nationality
FROM drivers

params.description: A canonical driver dimension: one row per driver with identifying name, reference, racing number, code, and nationality.
params.when_to_use: Look up driver display attributes (forename, surname) given a driverId. | Join driver attributes to race results, laps, pitstops, or season-level aggregates to add human-readable driver info. | Compose driver-centric reports (per-driver aggregates) where driver is the grain.
params.output_schema: driverId: unique driver identifier (derived from drivers.driverId) | forename: driver's given name (derived from drivers.forename) | surname: driver's family name (derived from drivers.surname) | driverRef: short string reference for the driver (derived from drivers.driverRef) | number: racing number assigned to the driver (derived from drivers.number) | code: three-letter code for the driver (derived from drivers.code) | nationality: driver's nationality (derived from drivers.nationality)
params.grounded_columns: drivers.driverId | drivers.forename | drivers.surname | drivers.driverRef | drivers.number | drivers.code | drivers.nationality
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to race_results_enriched on driverId — safe because drivers_name_nationality is one-row-per-driver and race_results_enriched is many-results-per-driver; joining this way will not duplicate driver rows but will expand by race_result rows (i.e., driver attributes will be repeated per result, which is intended when enriching results). | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to driver_lap_aggregates on driverId — safe because drivers_name_nationality is one-row-per-driver; driver_lap_aggregates is aggregated per driver (or per driver+race depending on that view's grain). If driver_lap_aggregates is aggregated at driver grain, the join preserves one-row-per-driver; if driver_lap_aggregates is at a finer grain (e.g., per driver+race), the join will produce multiple rows per driver corresponding to that finer grain (not duplication of aggregates at their own grain). | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to pitstop_aggregates on driverId — safe for the same reasons as driver_lap_aggregates. Ensure you understand the grain of the target aggregate before assuming one-row-per-driver result. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to season_driver_points or driver_season_rank on driverId (and season) — safe when you include season in the join keys because those views are season-level aggregates; the join will produce one row per driver+season as expected. | do NOT join without care to one-to-many tables/views such as race_results_enriched, qualifying_grid_positions, fastest_lap_per_race, or driver_running_points_by_season unless you intend to expand rows to that finer grain. Those joins will cause driver attributes to repeat across many rows but will not change the correctness of measures that are already aggregated at driver grain; however, if you start aggregating after such a join, you must re-aggregate (e.g., SUM/COUNT/DISTINCT) to avoid double-counting. | If you need to combine drivers_name_nationality with another one-to-many dataset and preserve driver-level measures, first aggregate the one-to-many dataset to driverId (and any additional grouping keys like season or raceId) so that the join is between datasets at compatible grains — this prevents multiplication of driver-level measures. | Joining to dimension tables such as constructor_dim should be done on the explicit key(s) those dims expose; drivers_name_nationality does not contain constructorId, so a join to constructor_dim is only possible via an intermediate view (e.g., race_results_enriched) that links driverId to constructorId. In that case, be mindful that the intermediate join may introduce multiplicity and re-aggregation is required if you want driver-level metrics.

views.name: drivers_with_dob_for_age
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  d.driverId,
  d.forename,
  d.surname,
  d.dob,
  -- age_years_expression: compute fractional years between dob and DATE('now') in SQL as (julianday('now') - julianday(dob)) / 365.25
  ((julianday('now') - julianday(d.dob)) / 365.25) AS age_years_expression
FROM drivers d
WHERE d.dob IS NOT NULL

params.description: Provides one-row-per-driver with date of birth and a computed fractional age in years (as of today).
params.when_to_use: Filter or report on drivers that have a known date of birth (e.g., find drivers within an age range). | Join driver identity and age information into race, season or result-level queries when you need driver age at query-time (current age). | Compose driver-level metrics that require age as an attribute (e.g., cohorting drivers by age group). | Enrich result-, race- or season-level data with driver demographics while preserving driver-level cardinality.
params.output_schema: driverId: unique identifier for the driver, derived from drivers.driverId | forename: driver's given name, derived from drivers.forename | surname: driver's family name, derived from drivers.surname | dob: driver's date of birth (non-null rows only), derived from drivers.dob | age_years_expression: fractional age in years computed as (julianday('now') - julianday(dob)) / 365.25; derived expression using drivers.dob and current date

params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to dimension or lookup views on their key columns — safe because races_row_level is one row per race (grain = raceId) so its attributes will not be duplicated when joined 1:1 or many:1 from the other side. | Safe: join to race_basic on raceId — e.g., JOIN race_basic rb ON races_row_level.raceId = rb.raceId — safe because race_basic is expected to be one-row-per-race (NORM sibling). | Safe: join to constructor_dim on constructorId or driver_dim on driverId only when the join is many-to-one from races to that dimension (i.e., if dimension keyed by that id) — typical use is joining via a derived linking table (like race_results_enriched) rather than directly to dimensions that are not keyed by raceId. | Do NOT join races_row_level directly to one-to-many fact/aggregate siblings (e.g., race_results_enriched, driver_lap_aggregates, pitstop_aggregates, fastest_lap_per_race, qualifying_grid_positions, season_driver_points, season_constructor_points, driver_running_points_by_season) without aggregating the many-side to race-level first, because those joins will multiply the race-level row and duplicate any race-level measures. | If you need measures from one-to-many tables, first aggregate those tables to raceId (for example: SELECT raceId, COUNT(*) AS entrants FROM race_results_enriched GROUP BY raceId) and then join that aggregated result to races_row_level ON raceId — this preserves the race-level cardinality and avoids measure duplication. | When composing multi-dimensional reports: (a) keep races_row_level as the driving table for race-level outputs; (b) left join aggregated facts (one row per race) to add metrics; (c) if you must join non-aggregated fact tables, include DISTINCT or window functions to reduce to raceId before joining. | Explicit example of unsafe join to avoid: JOIN race_results_enriched rre ON races_row_level.raceId = rre.raceId — this will produce one output row per race result, multiplying the race row for each participant and therefore duplicating any race-level attributes if not followed by aggregation.
